question: The government of India revised the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) in September 2021 by adding ________ drugs and deleting some.
solution:
The correct answer is __39.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government of India revised the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) in September 2021 by adding** 39 drugs** and deleting some.
 
• The government has released 384 medicines under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM). 
 
• Health minister **Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya **released the updated version of NLEM 2022 at an event in New Delhi, on September 13.
 
• The NLEM 2022 contains 384 medicines as compared to 376 in NLEM, 2015. 
 
• The medicines have now been categorized into 27 therapeutic categories. A new section has been added for medicines considered essential for the supportive management of COVID-19.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The NLEM **is a dynamic document and is revised on a regular basis considering the changing public health priorities as well as advancements in pharmaceutical knowledge.
 
• The National List of Essential Medicines was first formulated in 1996 and it has been revised thrice in **2003, 2011, and 2015.**
 
• The NLEM, **revised every three years,** was last updated in 2015 and a revision was delayed due to Covid-19.
 
• The NLEM committee headed by **Balram Bhargava**, director general of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), drafted a new NLEM.
